clue.text: Reprove a town for greed.

parts.note: to rap someone is to rebuke or reprove them
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Someone scolds a whole town for its avarice.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is grasping avarice, an aggressive wish to seize what others have.

clue.text: Moroccan Air Force overcomes loud rabble

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming over means sitting on top of the next piece

parts.note: the Riffs are the Berber people of the Rif mountains of Morocco
RAF is the Royal Air Force
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: North African airmen overpower a noisy mob.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'overcomes' puts RAF above F.
explanation.definitionFit: Riff-raff are disreputable common people, the mob.

clue.text: Fairylike pillars of the court?

explanation.surface: Delicate columns surrounding a palace courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: A peri is a fairy in Persian myth, so 'Fairylike' is read as peri-style.
explanation.definitionFit: A peristyle is a colonnade surrounding a courtyard; split as peri-style it means in the manner of a Persian sprite.

clue.text: Book-list. acceptable to a churchman

explanation.surface: A reading list approved by a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: The accepted list of books of scripture is the canon; a canon is also a cleric attached to a cathedral.

clue.text: First selector of course sells information

definitions.text: First selector of course sells information

parts.words: First selector of course sells information
parts.note: describes a racing pundit who picks the winner at the racecourse in advance and charges for the advice

explanation.surface: The leading picker at a racecourse sells what he knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a racecourse, not a meal or a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing pundit who sells predictions of winners picks horses before anyone else.

clue.text: Exploits old soldiers

explanation.surface: A note on how veterans are used and abused.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweat workers is to exploit them with long hours and low pay; old sweats are veteran soldiers.

clue.text: Engrossed "by ". command, regal variety

parts.note: a writ is a written legal command

indicators.note: a variety of something is another version of it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Absorbed by a royal order of a different kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges REGAL into LARGE. To engross a document is to write it out in large letters, which is the old sense of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To engross is to write out a document in large formal script, so the phrase means written in big letters.

clue.text: Yorkist leader in the islands of good Teutonic stock ?.

indicators.note: in places the initial inside the island name

parts.note: the Aran Islands lie off the west coast of Ireland

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Yorkist commander living in the islands has Germanic ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts Y inside ARAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The word was used, in now discredited racial theory, for people of supposed pure Germanic or Nordic descent.

clue.text: Belly-flop effect made by a big spender?

definitions.text: Belly-flop effect made by a big spender?

parts.words: Belly-flop effect made by a big spender?
parts.note: the spray of a bad dive, and also what a lavish spender makes by showing off with money

explanation.surface: A heavy diver's poor entry into a pool.
explanation.walkthrough: A big spender 'makes a big' one of these, spending showily; a belly-flop sends up one too.
explanation.definitionFit: Water thrown up by a body hitting it is spray; a showy display of spending is described with the same word.

clue.text: Without any, luck situation sounds bloody'

parts.note: in names a position, inside something

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word heard is spelt differently in the grid

parts.note: a vein is full of blood

explanation.surface: An unlucky position that seems gory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'situation sounds bloody' is IN VEIN, said like the answer, phrasing a place inside a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To try in vain is to try without success.

clue.text: Sacking fastener .. causes explosion

definitions.note: a phrase describing what the part does, standing for the part itself

parts.note: firing someone is sacking them from a job
a pin is a small fastener

explanation.surface: Losing a fastener on some sacking leads to a blast.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the thing by its job: the firing pin of a gun strikes the cartridge and sets off the charge.
explanation.definitionFit: In a firearm the striker that hits the primer and detonates the cartridge is called by this name.

clue.text: Poem idly, left in the rough -

indicators.note: rough, unshaped material suggests the letters before them are still to be put in order

explanation.surface: A verse written lazily and left unpolished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the rough' scrambles IDLY into IDYL; L for left follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a short pastoral poem describing a peaceful rural scene.

clue.text: Bow string rubber ?. No sir, that's crazy

indicators.note: crazy means the letters of the words before are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone offers a violinist something to rub on the strings and is told it is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's crazy' rearranges NOSIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosin is the resin violinists rub along their bow hair so it grips the strings.

clue.text: Railways out for singles to Wimbledon?

explanation.surface: Lines of track that don't count when two players meet on court.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; in singles play the outer side strips of the court, called by the same name as tram tracks, are out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tram tracks are rails; in tennis the narrow side lanes used only in doubles are out of play in singles.

clue.text: Carriage capsized at 'road crossing

parts.note: a fly was a light horse-drawn hired carriage
a boat that has capsized has turned over

explanation.surface: A coach overturned at a junction.
explanation.walkthrough: A fly is an old one-horse carriage for hire.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge carrying one road over another forms an elevated junction or crossing.

clue.text: Lover and, tune composer shows himself willing

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer is the verb offer oneself, or one who does

indicators.note: a composer puts notes together, so here the letters of the two words are set into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A romantic songwriter offers to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composer' rearranges LOVER and TUNE together. 'composer' looks like a person, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To come forward and offer to do something unasked is to show oneself willing.

clue.text: Hence six Roman kings?

parts.note: points to a Scandinavian country whose monarchs are numbered with Roman numerals, with several Haakons, Olafs and Magnuses reaching six or more

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about where half a dozen ancient rulers came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman' does not mean from Rome: it refers to the Roman numerals after royal names, as in Haakon VI.
explanation.definitionFit: This northern kingdom had kings such as Haakon VI and Magnus VI, whose numbers are written in Roman numerals.

clue.text: Go to work on this plant?

definitions.text: Go to work on this plant?

parts.words: Go to work on this plant?
parts.note: recalls the famous British advertising slogan 'Go to work on an egg', pointing to the egg plant

explanation.surface: Heading off to a job at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to work on an egg' was a well-known 1950s British Egg Marketing Board slogan; this vegetable is also called eggplant. 'plant' seems to be a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: The purple vegetable called eggplant in America is a plant whose fruit resembles a large egg.

clue.text: Ends gear-changing-that's disturbing

definitions.note: the clue's participle stands for the answer's verb sense, unsettling

indicators.note: changing means the letters of the preceding words switch places

explanation.surface: A clumsy gear change at the end of a journey is unsettling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges ENDSGEAR; 'gear-changing' reads as driving, but the hyphen hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into disorder or unsettle the mind, which is to disturb.

clue.text: Underground source of salt'? :

explanation.surface: Asking whether salt is dug from beneath the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is a room below ground; a salt cellar is the table pot that dispenses salt.

clue.text: Without this too, blank verse would be senseless.

definitions.text: Without this too, blank verse would be senseless

parts.words: Without this too, blank verse would be senseless
parts.note: blank verse lacks rhyme, and the idiom 'without rhyme or' the missing word means senseless

explanation.surface: A critic's remark that unrhymed poetry needs something more to make sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'without rhyme or reason' means senseless; blank verse already lacks rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Sense and logic are what this word names; the idiom pairs it with rhyme.

clue.text: Pools chance involving a million causes a quiver

indicators.note: involving means taking the next item inside, here a letter put within the bet's name

parts.note: the treble chance was a popular way of betting on the British football pools

explanation.surface: A punter shakes with excitement at the thought of a million-pound pools win.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools were a British weekly betting coupon on match results; the treble chance was its best-known bet. 'involving' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremble is a shaking movement, the same as a shiver or shudder.

clue.text: Day of sport night… of comedy

explanation.surface: Listing the entertainment, sporting by day and comic by night.
explanation.walkthrough: The Glorious Twelfth, 12 August, opens the British grouse-shooting season; Twelfth Night is a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelfth of August starts grouse shooting, and Shakespeare's comedy bears the same ordinal before Night.

clue.text: A government department perhaps all at sea ?

definitions.note: on a ship is one example of being at sea

parts.note: a board, such as the Board of Trade, was a British government department

explanation.surface: A ministry that seems completely confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all at sea' looks like confusion; here it means literally on a ship. 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers on a ship are on board, and being at sea is one case of that.

clue.text: Good idea for an electro encephalograph

explanation.surface: A clever thought about a hospital brain scanner.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden bright notion is a brainwave; an EEG machine records the electrical rhythms of the brain, also called brain waves.

clue.text: A manuscript — is included wrongly

indicators.note: included says the next word is placed inside the abbreviation

explanation.surface: Something has been wrongly slipped into a manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts IS inside MS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone astray or done in error has gone wrong.

clue.text: Deposit a jacket and hood

parts.note: to park something is to put it down and leave it

explanation.surface: Leaving one's coat and hood in the cloakroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a windproof coat with a hood attached.

clue.text: Bird tells BBC how to mark time

definitions.text: tells BBC how to mark time

explanation.surface: A bird gives the broadcaster instructions for the time signal.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC marks the hour with six short beeps called the pips, so 'pip it' is an instruction to sound them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipit is a small brown songbird; split as pip it, it orders the broadcast time signal.

clue.text: Suffer to remain

explanation.surface: Advice to put up with things and stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide can mean to tolerate or endure, and also to stay or continue living somewhere.

clue.text: Start season with this issue

parts.note: at the start of a race 'they're off', so off can mean starting
spring is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: Advice on beginning a new season with a particular matter on the agenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in the legal sense means a person's children, their descendants.

clue.text: Long to deprive a man of his father?

parts.note: the prefix de- signals removal or depriving, as in debone
a sire is a father, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: Asking how to separate a man from his dad.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as DE-SIRE, to remove a sire.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn or wish for it strongly.

clue.text: Put up with the closed shop

definitions.text: Put up with the closed shop

parts.words: Put up with the closed shop
parts.note: reads as tolerating a union-only workplace, but means panels raised over the windows of a shut store

explanation.surface: Tolerating a workplace where everyone must join the union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closed shop' suggests the trade-union arrangement; here it is simply a shop shut for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopkeepers fit hinged panels or roller blinds over windows when the premises close.
